text:
customer_alan: Hey team — we saw a ~30s burst last night that caused a bunch of 429s even though our dashboard shows we still had burst credits. Can you help explain why smoothing didn’t prevent it? Link to metrics: https://monitoring.example.com/teams/acme-app/runs/9876 :grimacing:

maria_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact timestamps (UTC) and an example request id? That’ll help us correlate with router logs.

customer_alan: Root span start ~2026-03-15T03:12:14Z -> 03:12:44Z. Example req id: req_0a9c. We were doing short LLM calls (max_tokens 64) at ~120rps for 40s, then spikes to 260rps for ~20s. Our client uses exponential backoff but saw ~20% 429s.

maria_support: Thanks. Quick explanation first — burst credits are a short-term cushion and the smoothing policy also applies debouncing. It’s possible to hit a combination of (1) credit consumption > refill during the spike and (2) router-level debounce that still rejects when concurrency/queue is saturated.

eli_sre: grabbing logs for req_0a9c now. FYI, the smoothing algorithm we run has a per-route token drain + an EWMA of request rate for the last 60s by default. If a single short spike exceeds the burst_bucket capacity and the backend queue tops out, you'll still see 429s even with some credits left due to inflation of concurrency across workers.

eli_sre: log snippet for req_0a9c:
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:22Z] router: request=req_0a9c route=/v1/completions user=acct-12345 -> throttle_reason=burst_bucket_depleted worker_queue_len=128 max_workers=128
[2026-03-15T03:12:22Z] infra: burst_bucket_before=12.4 burst_bucket_after=0.0 refill_rate_per_sec=0.2 smoothing_window=60
```

eli_sre: you can see burst_bucket_before low and then hit zero; refill_rate_per_sec is fractional (0.2 tokens/s) so a sustained 200rps will drain it quickly.

customer_alan: Wait — dashboard showed ~6 credits left at 03:12:20. Is that inconsistent?

maria_support: Dashboard credit numbers are rounded and sampled. Also there’s a subtlety: we maintain both a token count and an in-flight concurrency guard. The dashboard's "credits" column is the token bucket estimate at the sampling time; if many requests were in flight between samples they can consume more tokens faster than the UI shows.

sam_product: For context, the default burst_bucket size is proportional to plan and route history — short-lived telemetry noise can make it feel like credits should carry you. We've seen customers hit this when their spike is both high QPS and high concurrency (many parallel short calls).

maria_support: Quick repro checklist for you to try so we can rule out client-side issues:
1) Send the same load but limit client concurrency to 50 connections (not unlimited per process).
2) Add a small randomized jitter on retry (0-100ms) so retries don't synchronize.
3) If you need immediate fix, request an account-level smoothing increase (temporary) and we can bump your burst_bucket by +X for 1h.

customer_alan: How do we request that bump? Also is there a permanent config we can change?

maria_support: I’ve opened a support ticket and requested a temporary bump. Ticket #123456. For permanent controls you can:
- Set a per-route smoothing policy in the Console: smoothing.window_seconds (default 60) and smoothing.min_throughput.
- Increase reserved capacity via Dedicated or increase min_rate in the plan to get larger burst buckets.

sam_product: If you want to tune the smoothing window, decreasing it makes the system react faster to ramps (good for short bursts) but may increase variance; increasing it smooths over longer windows and can prevent transient rejections at the cost of slower scale-up. Typical values we see customers adjust to 30s for bursty short-ramp traffic.

eli_sre: Also note fractional refill behavior: our refill runs continuous but UI shows per-second rounded numbers. If you need precise accounting, we can dump the raw per-second refill logs. Example command for logs (internal):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SRE_TOKEN" \
  "https://internal-api.redwood.local/account/acct-12345/burst-logs?start=2026-03-15T03:10:00Z&end=2026-03-15T03:15:00Z"
```

customer_alan: Got it. We’ll try the concurrency cap + jitter test now. ETA 30m. Thanks for the ticket.

support_bot: Ticket created: #123456. Assigned to maria_support. ETA for temporary bump: 1 hour. :white_check_mark:

maria_support: Great — ping here after the test and we’ll iterate. If the cap + jitter removes the 429s, you likely need either larger burst_bucket or a client-side connection cap. If 429s persist we’ll run a deeper router trace and propose a config change.
